analysis.one_liner: SBI Life Insurance sells life insurance, savings, protection, pension and group policies across India, distributing mainly through SBI's bank branches and its own agency force.
analysis.whats_happening: SBI Life's next results (Q2 FY27, for the July-September 2026 quarter) are due on 28 October 2026 - less than two weeks away. In the last reported quarter (Q1 FY27, June 2026), profit after tax rose 22% YoY to about ₹725 crore and new business premium (APE) jumped 36% to ₹5,380 crore, but the Value of New Business (VNB) margin slipped to 26.2% from 27.4% a year earlier as group-term insurance, a lower-margin product, took a bigger share of the mix. The stock has been sliding for weeks and sits right at its 52-week low of ₹1,650, having fallen about 21% from its February 2026 peak.
analysis.plain_terms: This is India's largest private life insurer by premium, majority-owned by the State Bank of India. The business itself looks fine on growth: new policies sold are rising fast. The tension is that this growth is coming partly from cheaper, lower-margin group policies rather than the richer individual protection business, so the profitability of each new rupee of business sold has edged down even as the top line grows. Meanwhile the stock trades at a rich price relative to its book value and has fallen to a one-year low, so the market seems to be pricing in some of that margin worry already.
analysis.quarters: FY26 (year to March 2026): premium income rose 18.9% to roughly ₹99,956 crore, but net profit grew only 2.36% to about ₹2,470 crore - a sharp gap between topline and bottom line that is normal for a growing life insurer (new business carries upfront cost/reserving strain) rather than a one-off accounting distortion, but it means premium growth headlines overstate how fast profit is actually compounding. Q1 FY27 (June 2026): PAT up 22% YoY to ₹725 crore, VNB up 29% to ₹1,410 crore, but VNB margin down to 26.2% from 27.4%, which management attributed to a bigger mix of group-term business. Management has reiterated FY27 VNB margin guidance of 26-28%, and has flagged the GST exemption on life/health premiums (effective September 2025) as a transitional headwind affecting comparability of recent quarters - treat quarter-on-quarter premium comparisons around that period with caution.
analysis.performance_read: No splits or demergers are recorded for this stock, so the price series can be read at face value - this is not a corporate-action distortion. Over 5 years the stock is up 40.23% versus the Nifty's 25.27% and peer HDFC Life's -20.15%; over 3 years it's up 23.5% versus Nifty's 16.83% and the peer's -13%. So the long-run record is genuinely better than both the index and its closest listed peer. The uncomfortable part is the recent trend: the stock is down 9.62% over the last year (roughly in line with the Nifty) and sits at its 52-week low, 21.4% below its February 2026 peak - so recent momentum has reversed even though the multi-year story remains intact.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 65-70x and a price-to-book of about 8.5x, SBI Life is expensive by plain-vanilla standards, but P/E is not the right lens for an insurer - price-to-embedded-value and VNB multiples matter more, and embedded value grew 15% YoY to ₹80,790 crore with an operating return on embedded value near 19.7%, which is what the market is really paying for. Why it's priced this way: investors are backing continued double-digit new-business growth and margin resilience. Whether that's justified is a separate question - the margin has already compressed one quarter in a row, and if that trend continues the premium multiple looks harder to defend.
analysis.growth_read: Growth right now looks more volume-led than margin-led: APE (new premium) is up 36% YoY, far outpacing a VNB margin that actually fell from 27.4% to 26.2%. That combination - fast volume growth alongside margin compression - is the one flagged as less durable, since it suggests some of the growth is coming from writing more lower-margin group business rather than pure improvement in product mix or pricing power.
analysis.health_read: As a life insurer, SBI Life's balance sheet risk is less about debt and more about reserving and solvency: its solvency ratio stands at 1.90x against a regulatory minimum of 1.50x, a comfortable buffer. The more relevant risk here is business/product-mix risk - margin held up by premium guidance (26-28%) that has already seen one quarter of erosion - rather than any financial or leverage risk. There are no debt or pledge concerns on the promoter side.
analysis.ownership_read: State Bank of India is the promoter with 55.36% as of September 2026, and promoter pledge stands at 0% - a clean ownership structure. Foreign institutional investors hold about 20.95% and mutual funds about 15.87%. Not verified: a breakdown of which specific funds or individuals sit within those blocks; no single marquee individual investor stands out on the public shareholding pattern as currently reported - check Screener or the latest BSE/NSE shareholding filing for the granular list.
strengths: Value of New Business up 29% YoY to ₹1,410 crore in Q1 FY27
Embedded value up 15% YoY to ₹80,790 crore with operating return on EV of ~19.7%
Solvency ratio of 1.90x comfortably above the 1.50x regulatory minimum
Zero promoter pledge and a stable 55.36% SBI holding
watchpoints: VNB margin fell from 27.4% to 26.2% YoY in Q1 FY27 on a shift toward lower-margin group-term business
FY26 net profit grew just 2.36% even as premium income grew 18.9% - profit growth is lagging topline by a wide margin
Trades at roughly 8.5x book, among the pricier multiples in the sector, while the stock itself sits at a 52-week low
Q2 FY27 results due 28 October 2026 will show whether the 26-28% margin guidance is holding or slipping further
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results due 28 October 2026 - specifically whether the VNB margin stabilizes within the guided 26-28% band or continues the slide seen in Q1 FY27, which would confirm whether current growth is becoming more margin-dilutive over time.
analysis.data_notes: FY26 PAT (~₹2,470 crore, +2.36%) and embedded value (₹80,790 crore, +15%) figures were cross-checked across Business Standard, Kotak Neo and Equitybulls coverage of the company's own results release and were consistent. Valuation multiples showed a range across sources (P/E roughly 65-72x, P/B roughly 8.4-9.4x) - the figures used here reflect the central cluster, not an average of outliers. The exact composition of FII/mutual fund/individual holders within the shareholding pattern was not independently verified beyond aggregate category percentages - check Screener or the company's latest BSE shareholding filing for investor-level detail.
